newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia "happy" at EU enlargement decision.
newsitem.headline: Estonia "happy" at EU enlargement decision.

text.p: The tiny Baltic state of Estonia on Tuesday welcomed the European Commission's formal decision to recommend it and four other former Soviet bloc states and Cyprus for a first wave of European Union (EU) enlargement talks.
Along with Estonia, the EU executive agreed to invite Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovenia for early talks on entry to the trading bloc.
"We are very happy about the decision," foreign ministry spokesperson Ehtel Halliste told Reuters.
Estonia, which quit the former Soviet Union in 1991 along with Latvia and Lithuania, embarked on a radical course of market reforms and has long been viewed as the leader among the Baltic contenders.

The Commission also decided that Latvia and Lithuania, along with fellow EU candidates Bulgaria, Romania and Slovakia, are to be given so-called contractual accession partnerships to prepare for membership at their own pace.
